=== OWNER.md ===
# Continue the Ready request after the consumer update
The source brief and view changed since the retained first request. Refresh PLAR
against the actual source, preserving existing IDs, other asset history and the Start
control. Continue queue.ready through one newly reviewed request under this updated
contract and retain its resumable state. The original request belongs to the controlled
pixellab-test connection; inspect its actual current provider status before acting.
The connection supports one further controlled request in this stage. Preserve original
attempts and contracts. The assigned deliverable ends at the accepted revised request:
no image or renderer is supplied, no style is already approved, and integration and
art acceptance remain future work. Do not fabricate images, provider observations,
acceptance or a live-service identity. Work inside this consumer only.

=== STAGE.md ===
# Continue the existing Ready generation through delivery
The reviewed current queue.ready generation was submitted in the retained request
stage. Continue that same provider job and saved plan through actual retrieval, local
candidate import, mechanical/visual review and justified task finalization. Deliver the
reviewed PNG to the current PLAR destination and verify both real source consumers via
node verify-integration.mjs PATH (PATH is the selected PLAR delivery path).
The existing renderer obligations and family/style adoption are not silently completed
by this bounded Ready delivery. No runnable graphical renderer is supplied. Preserve
old source, plan, job, rejected-candidate and review history and all unrelated asset rows.
The controlled connection now exposes get_image and serves an actual synthetic PNG;
retain its identity/provenance and do not create another request. Inspect the downloaded
artifact itself. If a required candidate check fails, retain that result and report the
remaining correction instead of weakening criteria to pass. No upstream image or live
renderer acceptance is claimed by this assignment. STAGE.md extends the earlier OWNER
request-stage scope without rewriting the request's original bound source bytes.

=== BRIEF.md ===
# Asset brief

Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.

Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.

Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.

Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.

=== SOURCE-MAP.md ===
# Queue source map

src/queue.ts defines queue transitions; src/queue-view.ts maps states to visuals and supplies both full and compact status consumers. assets/ contains checked-in UI resources. Remote account badge data arrives at runtime. Read the code and BRIEF.md for actual behavior and scope.

// Execute the actual source consumers; this is not a renderer.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { stateAfter } from './src/queue.ts';
import { statusCell, compactStatus, display } from './src/queue-view.ts';
const expected = process.argv[2];
assert.ok(expected, 'Pass the selected PLAR delivery path');
const state = stateAfter('ok');
assert.equal(state, 'succeeded');
const consumers = [statusCell(state), compactStatus(state)];
for (const consumer of consumers) {
  assert.equal(consumer.path, expected);
  assert.equal(consumer.frames, 1);
}
const data = readFileSync(new URL(expected, import.meta.url));
assert.equal(data.subarray(0,8).toString('hex'), '89504e470d0a1a0a');
assert.deepEqual([data.readUInt32BE(16), data.readUInt32BE(20)], display.cell);
assert.equal(display.filter, 'nearest');
const hash = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
console.log(JSON.stringify({state, consumers, display, file: expected,
  sha256: hash(data), sources: Object.fromEntries(['src/queue.ts','src/queue-view.ts'].map(
    p => [p, hash(readFileSync(new URL(p, import.meta.url)))])),
  scope: 'Executed backend-to-view mapping and actual file/header lookup; no renderer, alpha compositing or artistic acceptance.'}, null, 2));

value.intent: One static 16x16 Ready status image for later destination assets/ready.png (consumer path). Transparent background, no fixed palette, partial alpha permitted (brief: transparent backgrounds, fixed palette not required). Checkmark motif, chunky strokes, cool blue near #70b9ed with a lighter highlight and no backing plate are specialist sample choices, revisable at style review.

intake.rationale: Concrete candidate interpretation for the reviewed scope; source requirements retain their original authority in the selected PLAR and packet.

value.intent: One static 16x16 Ready candidate for later assets/ready-confirmed.png. Required asymmetrical-arm check mark conveys success. Transparent background, full alpha permitted, no fixed palette. Cool blue accent relationship; Ready as representative sample is a specialist proposal, not approved style.

intake.rationale: Concrete candidate interpretation for the reviewed scope; source requirements retain their original authority in the selected PLAR and packet.

requirements.name: geometry
requirements.check: Decoded image is exactly 16x16 pixels with a single static frame (no horizontal strip, no extra canvas).
requirements.reason: Decoded PNG is 16x16 with one static frame; no strip or extra canvas.

requirements.name: transparent-background
requirements.check: The background is transparent: pixels outside the subject have alpha 0 and no opaque matte, box or fringe fills the cell. Partial alpha on subject pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.
requirements.reason: 227 pixels are RGBA 0,0,0,0; 29 subject pixels are opaque blue. Transparent exterior and open corners have no matte or fringe; no binary-alpha rule imposed.

requirements.name: ready-meaning
requirements.check: Viewed alone, Ready visibly uses a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion; it reads as completion rather than activity, failure, pause, or the idle Start control.
requirements.reason: Viewed native and 3x: a short descending left arm joins a distinctly longer ascending right arm into a clear check mark. It reads as successful completion rather than triangle, pause bars, loop or failure.

requirements.name: readability-1x-3x
requirements.check: Composited on #172336, the silhouette is readable at 1x and at 3x nearest-neighbor scale, with no essential detail lost into the panel colour.
requirements.reason: Native 16x16 panel composite shows a recognizable light-blue check; 48x48 nearest composite preserves clear steps and essential asymmetrical arms against #172336.

requirements.name: cool-blue-accent
requirements.check: The dominant colour treatment visibly relates to the existing UI's cool blue accent as seen in assets/start.svg (#70b9ed). This is a visual relationship judgement, not an exact-hex or palette-count rule.
requirements.reason: Visible sky-blue treatment relates directly to the preserved Start SVG's cool-blue cue; measured color happens to equal #70b9ed, but exact equality was not a rejection rule.

requirements.name: sample-pixel-craft
requirements.check: As a representative family sample, the image shows deliberate pixel-art construction: clean pixel clusters and edges, no noisy stray pixels, blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts, and a treatment that could plausibly be extended to Working, Retry and Paused.
requirements.reason: Viewed all native and enlarged views: compact connected stepped clusters form a crisp check without blur, isolated noise or downscaled illustration artifacts. A plausible sample for future family extension; family adoption and comparisons remain separate.

1	---
2	name: pixl
3	description: Use when delegating or producing PixelLab visual assets, including UI, sprites, animation, tiles, fonts, style consistency, inspection and project integration. Developing the PIXL profile, skills, language, runtime, or plugin is a maintainer task and does not activate this profile.
4	---
5	
6	For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.
7	
8	For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.
9	
10	For a retained production result, the delegation contract uses `pixl_plar_handoff` to save exact continuation data alongside your expert findings. Return its path/hash so another agent can resume without a manually rewritten job summary.
11	
12	The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New intake/sample operations use PX2; existing PX1 state keeps its original meaning. Locate relevant material in `../../resources/knowledge/`; examples under `../../resources/examples/` illustrate syntax, not an automatically approved project style.
13	
14	For repository-wide asset requirements, load [PLAR](../plar/SKILL.md), then select an asset from the consumer project's `plar.txt`. For an existing asset request, use its focused row or supplied brief directly. A selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate can use [PLAR preparation](../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed plan and durable request without handwriting PX2 records. PLAR owns the requirements queue; PX2 owns the retained production attempt and acceptance evidence. Keep actual source requirements stable when the queue status changes.
15	
16	Production uses the official paid PixelLab API, preferring the authenticated MCP tool surface. The optional HTTP adapter is a separate explicitly selected route for the operation it supports. Preserve existing user authorization and scope. Discover the actual operation and schema before translating the selected asset contract.
17	
18	Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.
19	
20	When imported library sources must survive kit updates, use [source retention and recovery](references/library-retention.md). Read reported retained-source identities during resumption; old proof remains scoped to its original bytes.
21	
22	Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.
23	
24	Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.
25	
26	Keep requirement authority through each translation: explicit user/project constraints, observations and proposals remain distinct in the provider request and review criteria. Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.
27	
28	Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.
29	
30	Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.
31	
32	Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.
33	
34	The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.
35	
36	The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.
37	
38	Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.
39	
40	Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.

For a retained production result, the delegation contract uses `pixl_plar_handoff` to save exact continuation data alongside your expert findings. Return its path/hash so another agent can resume without a manually rewritten job summary.

The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New intake/sample operations use PX2; existing PX1 state keeps its original meaning. Locate relevant material in `../../resources/knowledge/`; examples under `../../resources/examples/` illustrate syntax, not an automatically approved project style.

For repository-wide asset requirements, load [PLAR](../plar/SKILL.md), then select an asset from the consumer project's `plar.txt`. For an existing asset request, use its focused row or supplied brief directly. A selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate can use [PLAR preparation](../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed plan and durable request without handwriting PX2 records. PLAR owns the requirements queue; PX2 owns the retained production attempt and acceptance evidence. Keep actual source requirements stable when the queue status changes.

Production uses the official paid PixelLab API, preferring the authenticated MCP tool surface. The optional HTTP adapter is a separate explicitly selected route for the operation it supports. Preserve existing user authorization and scope. Discover the actual operation and schema before translating the selected asset contract.

Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.

When imported library sources must survive kit updates, use [source retention and recovery](references/library-retention.md). Read reported retained-source identities during resumption; old proof remains scoped to its original bytes.

Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.

Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.

Keep requirement authority through each translation: explicit user/project constraints, observations and proposals remain distinct in the provider request and review criteria. Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.

Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.

Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.

Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.

The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.

The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.

Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.

Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`, production `hash` as
`expect`, and your `details` object. CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return that file's path/hash as `handoff`; the caller opens it and compares its state
identity with fresh focused PLAR. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

=== handoff.py ===
"""Preserve a selected production continuation alongside the agent's own judgments."""

import json
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path

from . import graph, plar, store
from .codec import PixlError


def save(root, asset_id, requirements_hash, expect, details, path="plar.txt"):
    root = Path(root).resolve()
    if not isinstance(details, dict) or details.get("status") not in (
        "delivered", "partial", "needs_input", "blocked"
    ):
        raise PixlError("handoff_details", "details needs the agent's assignment status")
    if {"resume", "next", "asset_id", "requirements_hash", "version"} & details.keys():
        raise PixlError("handoff_details", "Derived fields belong to the snapshot; use caller_actions and future_work for commentary")
    selected = plar.read(root, path, asset_id)
    if selected["requirements_hash"] != requirements_hash:
        raise PixlError("handoff_stale", "Selected requirements changed; reread the asset")
    production = selected.get("production") or {}
    continuation = production.get("continuation")
    if not continuation:
        raise PixlError("handoff_state", "No production continuation is available; retain the allocation diagnostic in the ordinary result")
    if continuation["state_hash"] != expect:
        raise PixlError("handoff_stale", "Production state changed; reread before handing it back")
    document = {
        "version": 1,
        "asset_id": asset_id,
        "requirements_hash": requirements_hash,
        "resume": continuation,
        "next": continuation["action"],
        "selection": {
            "path": graph.confined(root, path).relative_to(root).as_posix(),
            "hash": selected["hash"],
            "current": production["selection_current"],
        },
        "details": details,
        "scope": "Snapshot of derived state plus agent-authored observations. No automatic contract, art or delivery acceptance; reread current PLAR before acting.",
    }
    data = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    digest = sha256(data).hexdigest()
    folder = graph.confined(root, ".pixl/handoffs")
    with store.lock(folder):
        target = graph.confined(root, f".pixl/handoffs/{digest}.json")
        if target.exists():
            if target.read_bytes() != data:
                raise PixlError("handoff_corrupt", "Retained snapshot bytes changed")
        else:
            store._atomic(target, data)
    return {
        "path": target.relative_to(root).as_posix(),
        "sha256": digest,
        "asset_id": asset_id,
        "requirements_hash": requirements_hash,
        "state_hash": expect,
        "next": document["next"],
        "scope": document["scope"],
    }

1	# Request and criteria handoff
2	
3	Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.
4	
5	## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract
6	
7	Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:
8	
9	- `version`: 1.
10	- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
11	- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
12	- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
13	- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
14	- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.
15	
16	Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.
17	
18	Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.
19	
20	Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.
21	
22	### Measured facts in creative requests
23	
24	Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.
25	
26	Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
27	`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
28	`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
29	A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
30	same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
31	are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.
32	
33	The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.
34	
35	## Resolve source evidence for the comparison
36	
37	For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
38	with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
39	--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
40	with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
41	invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
42	the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.
43	
44	When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
45	`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
46	reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.
47	
48	Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
49	`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
50	saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
51	locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
52	for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
53	mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.
54	
55	The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
56	labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
57	not an automatic grant of owner authority.
58	
59	## Caller: inspect before adopting
60	
61	Open the packet and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:
62	
63	1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
64	2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
65	3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
66	4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
67	5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.
68	
69	For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
70	sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
71	the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.
72	
73	1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
74	   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
75	   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
76	   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
77	2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
78	   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
79	   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
80	   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
81	3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
82	   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
83	   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
84	   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
85	   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
86	4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
87	   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
88	   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
89	   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
90	   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.
91	
92	For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
93	outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
94	untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
95	recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
96	preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.
97	
98	Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
99	quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
100	"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
101	cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.
102	
103	Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
104	establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
105	shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
106	reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
107	criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
108	to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
109	candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
110	condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
111	correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.
112	Do not call a corrected contract operable merely because its source locators resolve.
113	
114	When reviewing a specialist's response to a discrepancy, re-open the literal check.
115	An added attribution or a claim that a conventional construction excludes no valid
116	alternatives does not remove an unchanged mandatory recipe. Retain the source's
117	qualitative outcome as required and place the expert construction in a scoped proposal;
118	judge actual recognizability without declaring one geometric recipe universal.
119	
120	Resolve every evidence-report diagnostic before calling a locator verified. For a
121	text citation, open the actual source, use its file-local inclusive bounds and save
122	those bounds in the corrected packet; a nearby matching sentence does not repair a
123	wrong range. An unresolved named or visual reference needs actual inspection and a
124	recorded finding. A source hash alone never verifies the cited location or its meaning.
125	
126	The [delegation boundary](delegation.md#caller--specialist) distinguishes unchanged
127	historical evidence from the editable corrected proposal. A caller must not freeze
128	prior criterion text or authority in the new proposal; reassess those interpretations
129	against the source. Use the profile's visual-role distinctions when translating colour,
130	subject construction and transparency intent, rather than adding a construction rule.
131	
132	If a contract defect is found after delivery, preserve the original request, plan,
133	verdicts and candidate. Save a corrected proposal and independent comparison as a new
134	artifact, explicitly distinguishing it from the historical contract used for delivery.
135	Do not create another provider job merely to correct documentation, transplant old
136	verdicts to new criteria, or silently rewrite durable completed work. Carry both the
137	historical identity and the correction's adoption scope in the exact handoff details.
138	
139	Keep process requirements, output requirements and diagnostic proxies distinct. A required production route is checked through actual calls and downloaded-byte provenance; a property of the resulting image is evidence only when it establishes that claim. Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.
140	
141	Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.
142	
143	If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.
144	
145	If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.
146	
147	## Carry the comparison through production
148	
149	Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.
150

Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. # Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Resolve source evidence for the comparison

For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.

When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.

Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.

The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
not an automatic grant of owner authority.

## Caller: inspect before adopting

Open the packet and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:

1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.

For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.

1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.

For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.

Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.

Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.
Do not call a corrected contract operable merely because its source locators resolve.

When reviewing a specialist's response to a discrepancy, re-open the literal check.
An added attribution or a claim that a conventional construction excludes no valid
alternatives does not remove an unchanged mandatory recipe. Retain the source's
qualitative outcome as required and place the expert construction in a scoped proposal;
judge actual recognizability without declaring one geometric recipe universal.

Resolve every evidence-report diagnostic before calling a locator verified. For a
text citation, open the actual source, use its file-local inclusive bounds and save
those bounds in the corrected packet; a nearby matching sentence does not repair a
wrong range. An unresolved named or visual reference needs actual inspection and a
recorded finding. A source hash alone never verifies the cited location or its meaning.

The [delegation boundary](delegation.md#caller--specialist) distinguishes unchanged
historical evidence from the editable corrected proposal. A caller must not freeze
prior criterion text or authority in the new proposal; reassess those interpretations
against the source. Use the profile's visual-role distinctions when translating colour,
subject construction and transparency intent, rather than adding a construction rule.

If a contract defect is found after delivery, preserve the original request, plan,
verdicts and candidate. Save a corrected proposal and independent comparison as a new
artifact, explicitly distinguishing it from the historical contract used for delivery.
Do not create another provider job merely to correct documentation, transplant old
verdicts to new criteria, or silently rewrite durable completed work. Carry both the
historical identity and the correction's adoption scope in the exact handoff details.

Keep process requirements, output requirements and diagnostic proxies distinct. A required production route is checked through actual calls and downloaded-byte provenance; a property of the resulting image is evidence only when it establishes that claim. Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.

Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.

If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.

If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.

## Carry the comparison through production

Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.

The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.

Use CodeGraph first when the project has a `.codegraph/` index; otherwise use the host's code tools. Follow actual UI/renderer consumers through imports, manifests, loaders and backend state transitions. Group shared visual roles into one asset with multiple consumers. A function without an image does not automatically need one.
11	
12	Inspect existing art and the visible UI when available. Distinguish missing files, placeholders, reusable assets, visual mismatches and intentionally procedural/text-only elements. Note dynamic paths or unavailable modules in coverage.unresolved. Scope claims to the code and runtime actually inspected; a filename search is not exhaustive coverage.
13	
14	For each visual role, connect:
15	- Purpose and visible states to file/symbol/usage locations.
16	- Applicable canvas/frame geometry, projection, reference style, edge/alpha policy, timing, pivots, tile rules and import behavior to their sources.

Focused reads also return transitive dependency requirements/issues, actual source hashes, absolute project paths, visual references and a derived production view with pending jobs and acceptance state. Use that view to choose resumption versus new preparation; an editable status label is not production evidence. Pass the requirements_hash to a delegate; it changes with relevant requirements or source bytes, not unrelated queue progress. The portable CLI provides the same operations. Ordinary file editing is also supported; re-read and validate afterward.
24	
25	For refresh, read the queue before editing. Its changes report identifies drift and transitive dependents; after a save, or with `plar read --since PRIOR_HASH`, it compares authored requirements against retained history. Treat file-level impact as a prompt to inspect affected consumers, not proof every asset needs regeneration. Check the source overview and changed entry points for newly introduced consumers that no prior row could mention. Preserve unchanged requirements and existing IDs; distinguish a moved destination from a new visual role.
26	
27	A useful row can remain actionable with open questions. Resolve consequential unknowns for the selected action from the project, references or user; continue independent assets. Preserve stable IDs on refresh, retain superseded work as deferred with a reason, and inspect changed sources before deliberately updating their hashes. Update the queue after production and integration, linking retained evidence rather than copying provider job history.
28	
29	## Hand off to production
30	
31	For an asset request, continue through [PIXL](../pixl/SKILL.md) once the selected row is understood. A complete existing brief can go directly to production without a repository-wide scan. Give a delegated specialist the absolute project root, this skill/PIXL locations, PLAR path and asset ID, current user constraints and authorization, available references, and expected files/checks. Do not assume the child has the parent's conversation. Use the [shared delegation contract](../pixl/references/delegation.md) for caller questions and results.
32	
33	PIXL uses the authenticated **official PixelLab API**, through its exposed MCP tools or the supported HTTP adapter, for paid generation within the user's authorized work. Discover the actual operation schema and carry the selected requirements into its arguments. Existing authorization persists; ask only for a missing consequential choice or scope expansion. Development test settings belong to their harness and do not define production policy.
34	
35	For the first concrete candidate, use [selected-asset preparation](references/prepare.md): one local operation translates the reviewed contract into the existing PX2 plan and prepares its first durable request. Continue normal dispatch, retrieval and review through the host's actual PixelLab connection. Single-output preparation links its retained work into PLAR; inspect the allocation result and repair any concurrent-update conflict without duplicating the job. Reviewed changed requirements use the same operation's explicit revision path after pending work is resolved. `pixl_commit` accepts inline JSON, so a host need not encode and write a temporary wire file. Keep provider execution, returned bytes, visual judgment and engine integration distinct. Return actual delivered paths, review findings, integration status and the updated next action. An `integrated` label in PLAR is a caller claim, not runtime certification.

content.content:
1	# plar.txt format and operations
2	
3	Version 1 is UTF-8 JSON, not a new programming language. The normative shape is [plar.schema.json](../../../runtime/pixl/plar.schema.json). A complete worked project is [the queue UI example](../../../resources/examples/plar-project/README.md). Read its source before its example requirements.
4	
5	Top-level fields:
6	
7	| Field | Meaning |
8	| --- | --- |
9	| version | `1` |
10	| project | `name` and concise `brief`; no absolute installation paths |
11	| coverage | Arrays `included`, `excluded`, `unresolved`; explicit scan boundary and blind spots |
12	| sources | Stable `id`, project-relative `path`, optional `sha256`; saves bind existing files without a hash |
